pr_body:
Calling `torch.cuda.device_count()` before `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` is set to the desired value (during worker init) will lead to issues, as the env var will be read and persisted in memory, meaning later modifications will not affect it. This PR adds a way to obtain the device count without that issue.

FIX #4969
FIX #4981
pr_comments:
@Yard1 you can also try `torch.cuda._device_count_nvml()` , it will read `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` but will not cache the result.

it works in my case.

>   - TEST_DIST_MODEL=facebook/opt-125m DISTRIBUTED_EXECUTOR_BACKEND=ray pytest -v -s distributed/test_basic_distributed_correctness.py
>   - TEST_DIST_MODEL=facebook/opt-125m DISTRIBUTED_EXECUTOR_BACKEND=mp pytest -v -s distributed/test_basic_distributed_correctness.py

from `Distributed Tests` to `Distributed Tests (Multiple Groups)`, which is the case where we find the bug this time, tp=2 in 4 GPU machines.

### How would you like to use vllm

Below code will try to init LLM on the 1st GPU, causing GPU OOM.
```
from vllm import LLM

for i in range(8):
    llm = LLM(
        model="/models/mistral-7b",
        tensor_parallel_size=1,
    )
```
comments:
Hi @sfc-gh-zhwang, I don't think this is easily doable in vLLM at the moment within a single python process. Possibly you could construct each model on GPU 0 and move each to GPU X before moving on. 
I would recommend starting a separate process for each LLM and specifying `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` for each i.e. `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python script.py`, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 python script.py`, etc
Vllm always use cuda:0. That's bad. Same with #4981

review_comments: cuda_visible_devices can have more than 8 possible values :)

this will cache based on CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES input argument value, which generally should only be set twice (at the start and when initializing workers). We set the cache size a little higher than that just in case. The cache is also limited to the current running process.

I understand CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is set for several times in general. But I don't feel we should put a magic number here. Set the size to None will not cost infinite resource. It is dynamic (and can even save resource for you, because you typically don't set it for 8 times).

Sorry, I don't follow. Setting it to None will definitely not save any resources - the cache is not preallocated (it's just backed by a dict). The size of the cache is purely an implementation detail that will not change the logic. Indeed, we could just get rid of the cache altogether, if we were not concerned about performance. I disagree as a matter of principle for allowing any cache to grow infinitely, even if the chance of that is small. It can lead to multiple hard to debug memory leaks.
I'm surprised this already exists for quite a long time 🤣

Could this raise an exception if CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES doesn't exist? Maybe using `get` would be more safe
```suggestion
        return os.environ.get("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES")
```
this should never be reached if CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is not set (in that case, we do want the test to fail)
